t: Sack of Aleppo
c: The campaign ended in 962 with the Sack of Aleppo (962), which dealt a major blow to Sayf al-Dawla.

t: John I Tzimiskes overthrows Nikephoros Phokas
c: In 969, Nikephoros was overthrown by his subordinate, John I Tzimiskes.

t: Tzimiskes campaigns into Levant and Syria
c: By 975, Tzimiskes had campaigned far south into the Levant and Syria, pushing the borders away from Anatolia and extending Byzantine hegemony into Syria.

t: Death of Theodora ends Macedonian dynasty
c: The Macedonian dynasty came to an end with the death of Theodora in 1056, who had no children or heirs to replace her.

t: Turkish raid seizes Ani from Byzantium
c: In 1064, the first major Turkish raid crossed over into Armenia and Anatolia, seizing the city of Ani from Byzantium.

t: Death of Constantine X Doukas
c: In 1068, the emperor Constantine X Doukas died with only two children who had not come to maturity to succeed him.

t: Byzantine army sent against Roussel
c: In 1074, the empire sent an army against him led by Ioannes Doukas and Andronikos Doukas.

t: Alexios I Komnenos sent to capture Roussel
c: In 1075, the imperial court sent a new general, Alexios I Komnenos to apprehend him.

t: Alexios I Komnenos becomes emperor
c: In 1081, Alexios Komnenos successfully led a coup against the government and became emperor.

t: Crusaders besiege Antioch
c: In 1098, the Crusaders made their way to Antioch and laid siege to it.

t: Alexios defeats Bohemond
c: In 1108, Alexios finally defeated Bohemond, who returned to Italy, but failed to return Antioch to Byzantine hands.

t: John II Komnenos succeeds Alexios
c: Alexios was succeeded by his son John in 1118.

t: Manuel I Komnenos succeeds John II
c: John was succeeded by his son Manuel Komnenos in 1143.

t: Manuel and Kilij Arslan II establish truce
c: By 1162, Manuel and Kilij Arslan II established a truce which allowed Manuel to focus his attention elsewhere.

t: Death of Manuel I, Komnenian decline
c: The Komnenian dynasty declined when Manuel I died in 1180 and came to an end in 1185 with the fall of Andronikos I Komnenos.

t: Alexios III Angelos usurps throne
c: He was usurped in 1195 by Alexios III Angelos.

t: Sinop captured from Trapezuntine Empire
c: Trapezuntine Empire also suffered loss as well, as Sinop was captured in 1214 and again, definitively in 1265 to Mu'in al-Din Parwana.

t: Bayezid I captures Philadelphia

t: Mehmed II conquers Constantinople
c: In 1453, the empire finally fell to the Ottomans under Mehmet II.

c:

t: Early Cycladic II period begins
c:
Early Cycladic II (ECII)

The Keros-Syros culture is named after two islands in the Cyclades: Keros and Syros.

t: Early Cycladic III period begins

Minoan civilization develops from Neolithic culture
c: The Minoan civilization developed from the local Neolithic culture around 3100 BC, with complex urban settlements beginning around 2000 BC.

Protopalatial society emerges in Middle Minoan I
Population surge at Knossos, Phaistos, and Malia

t: Study confirms Minoan-modern Greek continuity
c: (2014) published in Anthropologischer Anzeiger also indicated craniological similarities between modern Greeks and Minoans, indicating continuity.

t: Genetic study shows Minoan-Mycenaean similarity
c: (2017) found that Minoans and Mycenaean Greeks were genetically highly similar – but not identical – and that modern Greeks descend from these populations.

t: Mycenaean Greece declines during Bronze Age
Draco establishes legal code in Athens
c: After a failed coup led by Cylon of Athens around 636 BC, Draco was appointed to establish a code of laws in 621.

t: Peace treaty negotiated by Nicias
c: After the deaths of Cleon and Brasidas, the strongest proponents of war on each side, a peace treaty was negotiated in 421 by the Athenian general Nicias.

t: Athens and Argos defeated at Mantinea
c: In 418 BC allied forces of Athens and Argos were defeated by Sparta at Mantinea.

t: Athens wins Battle of Cyzicus
c: Initially the Athenian position continued relatively strong, with important victories at Cyzicus in 410 and Arginusae in 406.

t: Thebes defeats Sparta at Leuctra
c: By 371 BC, Thebes was in the ascendancy, defeating Sparta at the Battle of Leuctra, killing the Spartan king Cleombrotus I, and invading Laconia.

t: Messenia gains independence from Sparta

t: Battle of Mantinea
c: The rising power of Thebes led Sparta and Athens to join forces; in 362 they were defeated by Thebes at the Battle of Mantinea.

t: Death of general Epaminondas

t: Philip defeats Greek alliance at Chaeronea
c: In 338 BC, he defeated a Greek alliance at the Battle of Chaeronea, and subsequently formed the League of Corinth.

t: Alexander leads expeditions to Bactria and India
c: From 329 BC he led expeditions to Bactria and then India; further plans to invade Arabia and North Africa were halted by his death in 323 BC.

t: Aegean Islands added to Roman territory
c: The Aegean Islands were added to this territory in 133 BC.

t: Antikythera mechanism created
c: The Antikythera mechanism, a device for calculating the movements of planets, dates from about 80 BC and was the first ancestor of the astronomical computer.

t: Draco establishes earliest laws of Athens
c: The earliest laws of Athens were established by Draco, in 621/0; his law on homicide was the only one to have survived to the Classical period.

t: Cypselus becomes tyrant of Corinth
c: The earliest Greek tyrant was Cypselus, who seized power in Corinth in a coup in 655 BC.

t: Olympic Games revived
c: According to Greek tradition the first games at Olympia had been established by Heracles, but these had fallen out of practice until they were revived in 776…

t: Antiochus III defeated at Thermopylae and Magnesia
c: The perceived weakness of Macedonia in the aftermath of these conflicts encouraged Antiochus III the Great of the Seleucid Empire to invade mainland Greece,…

t: Demetrius seizes Macedonian throne after Cassander
c: After Cassander's death in 298 BC, however, Demetrius seized the Macedonian throne and gained control of most of Greece.

t: Pyrrhus campaigns against Rome in Italy
c: Pyrrhus' armies also attempted an assault against the state of Ancient Rome during their unsuccessful campaign in what is now modern-day Italy in 280-275 BC.

t: Death of Antigonus II of Macedon
c: Antigonus II ruled until his death in 239 BC, and his family retained the Macedonian throne until it was abolished by the Romans in 146 BC.

t: Chremonidean War begins in Greece
c: In 267 BC, Ptolemy II persuaded the Greek cities to revolt against Antigonus, in what became the Chremonidean War, after the Athenian leader Chremonides.

t: Aetolian League gains control of Thebes
c: The Aetolian League was restricted to the Peloponnese, but on being allowed to gain control of Thebes in 245 BC became a Macedonian ally.

t: Demetrius captures Athens
c: To counter the power of Macedon under Cassander, Athens courted alliances with other Hellenistic rulers such as Antigonus I Monophthalmus, and in 307 Antigonus…

t: Athens defeats Macedon with Ptolemaic aid
c: After Demetrius captured Macedon, Athens became allied with Ptolemaic Egypt in an effort to gain its independence from Demetrius, and with Ptolemaic troops…

t: Athens establishes Ptolemaia cult for Ptolemaic Kingdom
c: Athens rewarded the Ptolemaic Kingdom in 224/223 BC by naming the 13th phyle Ptolemais and establishing a religious cult called the Ptolemaia.

t: Antigonus II dies, Achaean League revolts
c: Antigonus II died in 239 BC.

t: Death of Demetrius II, Philip V becomes king
c: Antigonus's son Demetrius II died in 229 BC, leaving a child (Philip V) as king, with the general Antigonus Doson as regent.

t: Philip V becomes king of Macedon

t: First Macedonian War breaks out
c: The First Macedonian War broke out in 212 BC, and ended inconclusively in 205 BC, but Macedon was now marked as an enemy of Rome.

t: Rome defeats Carthage
c: In 202 BC, Rome defeated Carthage, and was free to turn her attention eastwards, urged on by her Greek allies, Rhodes and Pergamum.

t: Second Macedonian War breaks out

t: Flamininus declares Greek cities free
c: At the Isthmian Games in 196 BC, Flamininus declared all the Greek cities free, although Roman garrisons were placed at Corinth and Chalcis.

t: Rome declares war on Seleucid Antiochus III
c: In 192 BC, war broke out between Rome and the Seleucid ruler Antiochus III.

t: Romans defeat Antiochus III at Magnesia
c: During the course of this war Roman troops moved into Asia for the first time, where they defeated Antiochus again at Magnesia on the Sipylum (190 BC).

t: Peace of Apamaea establishes Roman dominance
c: The Peace of Apamaea (188 BC) left Rome in a dominant position throughout Greece.

t: Perseus succeeds Philip V of Macedon
c: When Philip V died in 179 BC, he was succeeded by his son Perseus, who like all the Macedonian kings dreamed of uniting the Greeks under Macedonian rule.

t: Greek peninsula becomes Roman protectorate
c: In 146 BC, the Greek peninsula, though not the islands, became a Roman protectorate.

t: Pompey the Great defeats Mithridates
c: Mithridates was finally defeated by Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus (Pompey the Great) in 65 BC.

t: Augustus annexes Greece as province of Achaea
c: Finally, in 27 BC, Augustus directly annexed Greece to the new Roman Empire as the province of Achaea.

t: Fourth Macedonian War ends, Macedonia defeated

t: Constantine the Great founds Constantinople

t: Roman Empire divides into East and West

t: Achaean League allies with Rome
c: In the Second Macedonian War the Achaean League allied with Rome against Macedonia in 197 BC.
